title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a typed page numbered '- 168 -' and headed 'IX'. It is not part of the handwritten divided-power De Rham notes around it. It appears to be a typescript page of SGA 7 I, Exposé IX (Grothendieck, 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie'), from the section on the complex-analytic analogue of the theory. It was presumably reused or inserted into this folder.

Context (13.1.3): for a smooth relative analytic group A over a complex analytic space S with connected fibres, there is an exponential exact sequence 0 → R → E = Lie(A/S) → A → 0. Here E is a locally free vector bundle and R is an analytic subgroup of E that is étale over S.

13.1.4: this sequence is functorial in A and commutes with base change. It therefore gives an equivalence of categories, compatible with base change, between:
- smooth relative analytic groups with connected fibres; and
- pairs (E, R), with E a locally free bundle and R ⊂ E an étale analytic subgroup.
The inverse functor is (E, R) ↦ E/R.

13.1.5: call A 'abéloïde' if it is smooth, proper and separated with connected fibres, so A = A°. Then R is a local system of free Z-modules whose rank at s is 2·rank_s(E), and conversely. Equivalently, A is a family of complex tori. It is described by a local system R together with a complex-analytic vector bundle structure on the real-analytic bundle R ⊗_Z ℝ. No polarization is assumed, so these are families of complex tori, not necessarily abelian.

13.2 begins formal completion along a fibre. Fix s ∈ S and let S_n be its n-th infinitesimal neighbourhood. For X over S put X_n = X ×_S S_n. The inductive system (X_n) is the formal completion X̂ of X along X_s. It is functorial in X and commutes with projective limits.

The purpose, in SGA 7 IX, is to compare analytic and formal structures of degenerating abelian varieties and Néron models near a point of the base.
errors: No mathematical error. The converse in 13.1.5 needs R to be a lattice fibrewise, i.e. R ⊗ ℝ ≅ E. This is automatic, since a discrete subgroup of rank 2g in C^g is a lattice, and properness supplies the discreteness. The text leaves this implicit.
